creditRules.note: Academic coursework counts 1 clock hour = 1 AASECT CE hour (a 3-credit semester course = 45 clock hours). AASECT sponsored/approved CE = 1:1. Non-AASECT CE (APA, NCHEC, ACCME, etc.) counts at half value. Final acceptance is at the discretion of the AASECT Certification Committee.

applicantNote: Applicants are held to the requirements in effect when they enter into a supervision contract (or may choose the most recent requirements).

sources.title: AASECT Requirements for Sex Therapist Certification

terms.clientWork: clinical treatment of clients with sexual concerns

requirements.label: Core knowledge
requirements.longLabel: Human Sexuality Education: Core Knowledge Areas

areas.label: Ethics and ethical behavior
Developmental sexuality from a bio-psycho-social perspective across the life course
Socio-cultural and familial factors in relation to sexual values and behaviors
Sexual orientation and/or gender identity
Intimacy skills, intimate relationships, interpersonal relationships and family dynamics
Diversities in sexual expression and lifestyles (relationship structures, sexually diverse communities)
Sexual and reproductive anatomy/physiology
Health/medical factors that may influence sexuality
Range of sexual functioning and behavior, from optimal to challenging
Sexual exploitation, including sexual abuse, sexual harassment and sexual assault
Sexuality and technology (e.g., social media, generative AI)
Substance use/abuse and sexuality
Pleasure enhancement skills
Learning theory and its application
Professional communication and personal reflection skills
History of the discipline of sex research, theory, education, counseling and therapy
Principles of sexuality research and research methods

countingNotes: At least 3 clock hours documented in each of the 17 CKAs.
Remaining hours may be spread among CKAs, maximum 20 hours in any one CKA; hours above 20 in a CKA do not count toward the 90.
15 of the 90 hours must be synchronous (in person or virtual).
CKAs G, H, K and L are time sensitive.
Core Knowledge and skills training are documented separately; the same hour is not counted in both.

requirements.label: Sex therapy training
requirements.areaTerm: Sex Therapy Skills Training content area

areas.label: Theory and methods of sex-related psychotherapy, including several different models
Techniques of sex-related assessment and diagnosis of the DSM "Psychosexual Disorders"
Intervention in relationship systems experiencing sex and intimacy problems
Medical intervention in the evaluation and treatment of psychosexual disorders
Principles of consultation, collaboration, and referral
Ethical decision-making and best practice

conditional.label: couples counseling training
conditional.question: hasCouplesTraining
conditional.note: Therapists with no documented graduate or postgraduate training in couples counseling must acquire 16 hours of couples counseling training as part of the 60 hours.

countingNotes: At least 3 hours in each content area A–F, maximum 20 hours in any one content area.
30 of the 60 hours must be synchronous through an academic sex therapy program, a comprehensive sex therapy program, or AASECT approved sex therapy training.
Training must teach specific sex therapy techniques and interventions, not just theory.
Up to 5 additional supervision hours (beyond the 50) may be applied to skills training; they cannot also count as supervision.

requirements.label: Supervision

alternative.question: tenYearsSexTherapy
alternative.label: 10+ years of post-degree sex therapy practice (average 20 hours/week)
alternative.note: Requires an endorsement of clinical skill history by an AASECT Certified Sex Therapist; 18-month minimum still applies.

countingNotes: Supervision must be with an AASECT Certified Sex Therapist Supervisor under a signed supervision contract; hours before the contract do not count.
Minimum 25 individual (one-to-one) hours, 20 of them with a Primary Supervisor; remaining 25 may be individual or group.
Supervision spans at least 18 months, maximum 6 hours per month.

requirements.label: SAR
requirements.longLabel: Attitudes and Values Training Experience (e.g., Sexuality Attitude Reassessment)
countingNotes: Minimum 14 clock hours of structured group, process-oriented experience (e.g., a SAR).
The SAR must be AASECT sponsored or approved; the applicant must have attended (not facilitated).
May be virtual or in person.
Applicant also submits a 1-page therapy philosophy (completed outside NWIOI).

outside.question: hasClinicalDegree
outside.label: Advanced clinical degree that included psychotherapy training, plus 2 years (master's) or 1 year (doctoral) of post-degree clinical experience

outside.question: hasLicense
outside.label: A valid state license or certificate to practice psychotherapy independently (psychology, medicine, social work, counseling, nursing, or MFT)

outside.question: clinicalHoursUnderContract
outside.label: 300 hours of clinical treatment of clients with sexual concerns while under an AASECT supervision contract

outside.question: aasectMember
outside.label: AASECT membership (Early Career Professional, Professional, Retired, or Emeritus), maintained throughout supervision
Application materials: therapy philosophy statement, supervisor and colleague endorsement letters, and the AASECT application fee
